expectations.text: Rejects page views as the headline KPI, stating it measures demand, not quality.
expectations.evidence: 'Views measure demand, not quality.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 70% helpful target because it comes from a vendor blog, and sets targets from each page's own baseline.
expectations.evidence: 'A docs-tooling vendor's blog isn't your baseline... set per-page targets from it.'

expectations.text: Treats "was this helpful" votes as triage only, because votes are not validated against task success.
expectations.evidence: 'Votes are triage only. They aren't validated against whether the reader finished the task.'

expectations.text: Recommends executable steps passing in CI against the released product as the first signal, with a wiring cost of about half a day then near-zero, as the use of the platform engineer's day.
expectations.evidence: 'Add this first... Setup is about half a day, then near zero upkeep.'

expectations.text: Recommends tickets and issues that cite a page or its task as the second signal (near-zero to collect, a standing job to read), each pointing at a wrong or ambiguous step or a missing variant.
expectations.evidence: 'It costs almost nothing to collect, and each ticket points at a wrong, ambiguous or missing step.'

expectations.text: States the efficiency ordering out loud: CI pass > cited tickets > search refinements > helpful votes > task test > page views.
expectations.evidence: The full efficiency ordering is not stated.

expectations.text: States the value ordering out loud: task test > CI pass > cited tickets > search refinements > helpful votes > page views.
expectations.evidence: The full value ordering is not stated.

expectations.text: Rejects quarterly moderated task tests on all 40 pages and promotes the task test only for the three top-traffic pages.
expectations.evidence: 'Run the moderated task test on the top three pages'.

expectations.text: Treats the restore page's ticket drop with no other change as a reason to promote a task test, because silence can also mean readers gave up, rather than as proof the page is fine.
expectations.evidence: 'silence can also mean readers gave up'. Restore 'goes first in the task-test rotation'.

expectations.text: Labels the wiring costs as estimates, not measurements.
expectations.evidence: 'Its wiring costs are estimates, not measurements.'

expectations.text: Prescribes per-page drift metadata: `owner` as a team, `tested_with` as the API version or run date for the unversioned product, and `last_verified`.
expectations.evidence: Stamp all 40 pages with owner (a team), tested_with (a run date) and last_verified.

expectations.text: Sets the stale-page job to flag `last_verified` older than one quarter for the unversioned hosted product and labels that threshold a baseline to tune to the release cadence.
expectations.evidence: 'older than one quarter' is given, but it is not labelled a baseline to tune to cadence.

expectations.text: Requires the CI job to assert the documented output, not just the exit code, and to run on a schedule as well as on docs commits.
expectations.evidence: 'Assert the documented output, not just the exit code... Run it on a schedule, not only on docs commits.'

expectations.text: Adds a path-based code-owner rule so changes to CLI flags, API schemas or config keys request a docs review.
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned.

expectations.text: Recommends a periodic cull of pages with neither traffic nor an owner.
